title: Are four attempts four chances?
hook: Compare independent attempts with four copies of one shared outcome.

doesNotKnow: Four independent attempts each succeed with probability .25. Is at-least-one success above .5?

misconception: The primary and materially changed case must have the same consequence.
objective: Compute the pass at k construction and explain its countercase and stated boundary.

claims.text: Four independent attempts gave .68359375 probability of at least one success. Sharing one draw left it at .25; two independent attempts gave .4375. Repeating shared outcomes supplied no extra chance. This is oracle success: without a checker, it does not identify which answer to choose.
